investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC (curl, plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication/browser) against the venue's own official '/agenda/' page and one per-event detail page, followed by a genuine Level 2 STRUCTURAL check of this WordPress site's own /wp-json/ REST route index once Level 1 left the full event date (day+month, but never a year) unresolved.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://petitbain.org/agenda/ returned this venue's own bespoke WordPress theme ('petitbain') custom-post-type 'evenement' archive, containing 59 static event cards (all 59 cleanly parsed by this investigation's own extraction across both of this theme's card sub-templates). Each card states its own WordPress post ID, first-party detail-page URL, title(s), and a 'weekday day month-name' date string — but NEITHER the agenda list NOR a sampled per-event detail page (https://petitbain.org/evenement/boris/) ever states a year anywhere in first-party page content. The venue's own page-level JSON-LD (WebPage/BreadcrumbList/WebSite) carries no Event data and no year context either. Escalated to Level 2 to check whether a structured JSON path might expose the missing year (and price/time).

Fetched this WordPress site's own /wp-json/ REST route index (238 registered routes). No 'wp/v2/evenement' custom-post-type REST route is registered (direct request to /wp-json/wp/v2/evenement returned HTTP 404 — confirmed live, not merely absent from the index). The only event-adjacent registered namespace, '/pys-facebook/v1/event', is a POST-only Facebook-Pixel conversion-tracking endpoint (PixelYourSite plugin: args are event/data/ids/eventID/woo_order/order_key/referrer_url — a client-side analytics callback, not an event-data feed) — confirmed by a direct GET (HTTP 404, correctly rejecting the wrong method) and by its own documented args in the route index. No better structured data path exists; the static agenda page itself remains the only public event-data path, and it never states a year.

venue_reference: Petit Bain (floating venue/barge moored at 7 Port de la Gare, 75013 Paris, near the Bibliothèque François Mitterrand)

identity.notes: The retained agenda page's own <title> reads 'Agenda | Petit Bain – Équipement culturel flottant' ('floating cultural facility') at the venue's own domain petitbain.org. The retained page's own footer directly states the venue's own address: '7 Port de la gare - 75013 Paris' — matching the assigned venue address exactly. Every image asset is self-hosted under petitbain.org/wp-content/.

site_classification.platform: WordPress, bespoke theme 'petitbain' (wp-content/themes/petitbain/), custom post type 'evenement', NOT exposed via wp-json REST. Every event is a static, repeated HTML card ('unevt post-{ID} evenement ...') directly on the agenda archive page itself — no client-side rendering or pagination needed to see the full (currently 59-event) listing. Ticket purchase, where present, redirects to a third-party ticketing domain (billetterie.seetickets.fr) whose own outbound URL slug happens to include a full date with year (e.g. '20-octobre-2026') — noted for transparency, but this policy treats a third-party domain as a discovery lead, not first-party fact authority, so it is NOT used to complete this source's own date field.

title.notes: Each card's own first '<span class="titartprog">' (concert-template cards) or '<div id="nomsoiree">' (soirée/club-template cards) text, stated directly.

start_date.notes: Each card's own '#ladatevtmin' div directly states a weekday abbreviation + day + French month name (e.g. 'mar 20 octobre') — but genuinely NEVER a year, on the agenda list OR on the sampled per-event detail page (https://petitbain.org/evenement/boris/, checked explicitly). No page/section heading anywhere on either retained page states a year either (the page's own JSON-LD 'datePublished'/'dateModified' metadata fields are page-authoring timestamps, not event dates, and were not used). A year could only be produced here by AI plausibility reasoning (e.g. 'today is August 2026, so a card showing October is probably this October') — exactly the AI_INFERENCE the policy prohibits from ever reaching PROVEN — so this stays honestly PARTIAL with no claimed value, never fabricated.

time.notes: No time-of-day is stated anywhere on the list card or the sampled detail page.

end.notes: No end-time or end-date is stated anywhere on either the list card or the sampled detail page.

venue_location.value: Petit Bain, 7 Port de la Gare, 75013 Paris
venue_location.notes: Single-venue source. The retained page's own footer directly states the full address ('7 Port de la gare - 75013 Paris').

source_record_id.notes: Each card's own root element class attribute carries 'post-{ID}' (e.g. 'post-10537') — this theme's own WordPress post ID, a standard structural convention of the CMS itself, directly exposed on every card, the same class of documented CMS-ID convention already accepted for Le Trianon's data-id.

event_url.notes: Each card's own anchor 'href', stated directly — this venue's own first-party detail page.

price.notes: No price is shown on the list card or the sampled detail page. Where ticketing exists at all it redirects to the third-party billetterie.seetickets.fr checkout domain (and is entirely absent — the outbound link is HTML-commented-out — for sold-out shows), which this policy does not treat as first-party price authority.

blockers.description: start_date can only ever reach PARTIAL (day+month, no year) from this source's own first-party pages. This is a genuine, honest limitation of the source itself, not a parsing gap — no first-party page anywhere states a year. Downstream Event resolution will need its own policy for handling a day/month-only Observation (e.g. combining with a separately-governed external signal) rather than this collector ever inventing one.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (page title, footer address, self-hosted asset URLs).

A CONFIRMED public data path retained: the agenda archive page itself, exposing all 59 currently-listed events at once.
title, venue_location, source_record_id, and event_url are all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE.

start_date is honestly PARTIAL (not fabricated to PROVEN) because this source's own first-party pages never state a year anywhere — recording this honestly, per policy, means READY_FOR_ACTIVATION's activation gates are not attempted here even though they would technically not be blocked by a PARTIAL start_date; READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF is the honest, calibrated next step instead.

A bespoke collector family is required (NEW_FAMILY_REQUIRED): this theme's own card markup ('unevt'/'ladatevtmin'/'titevtprog'/'titartprog'/'nomsoiree') does not match any existing reusable family, including the superficially similar ingestion/wp-evenement-cards/ (Le Trianon/Élysée Montmartre), whose cards always state a full day+month+YEAR string.
